# fastapi-stream-lease

> Distributed stream and SSE concurrency lease manager for FastAPI and Starlette backed by atomic Redis Lua scripts.

FastAPI Stream Lease limits active streams instead of requests per minute. It is useful
for SSE, LLM token streaming, WebSocket sessions, and other long-lived HTTP responses
that can hold a worker socket or upstream API budget.

## What it solves

- Per-user and global concurrent stream limits.
- Atomic Redis Lua acquire, renew, release, and expiration cleanup.
- HTTP 429 before upstream token generation starts.
- Upstream generator closure when the downstream client disconnects.
- Redis Cluster hash tags, Sentinel coverage, circuit breaker, and fail-open or fail-closed policies.
- Prometheus and OpenTelemetry metrics for active leases.

## Common questions

### How do I limit concurrent SSE connections in FastAPI?

Wrap the async token generator with `manager.stream(user_id, token_stream())`. The lease
is acquired before the response starts and released when the stream finishes, fails, or
the client disconnects.

### How is this different from a rate limiter?

A rate limiter counts requests in a time window. A stream can stay open for 30 to 60
seconds, so one user can hold several worker sockets while sending only a few requests.
This library limits concurrent open streams.

### Does it work with LLM token streams?

Yes. It wraps any async token generator, including OpenAI, Anthropic, LiteLLM, or a
provider-specific SDK.

### What happens if Redis is unavailable?

The default is fail-closed: the API returns HTTP 503 instead of allowing unlimited
streams. `LeaseConfig(fail_open=True)` enables worker-local fallback leases during an
outage.

### Is it production-ready?

The project is pre-1.0. Version `0.6.x` has production-focused failure handling, Redis
Cluster and Sentinel coverage, and 100% statement and branch coverage. Pin a version and
test your own failure modes before a broad rollout.
